hypothesis: At N=256 (data_seed 0, fresh seeds 24-26, 4 layers, d_model=64, e in [0, 0.5], m2 in [0.1, 1], 3000 steps, best-of-3 controls), the force-margin decline relative to N=128 comes from the random controls rather than from the trained model. Trained best-layer force R2 stays within 0.02 of the same seed's N=128 value (paired arm proposed this cycle), while the force control R2 rises by >= 0.03. All values are read from run-record probes_final and trajectories (unrounded). Paired differences are computed per seed against the N=128 seeds 24-26 arm; if that arm is unavailable, the comparison is reported as not computed.
expected_if_true: In >= 2 of 3 seeds: |trained force R2(N=256) - trained force R2(N=128)| <= 0.02 AND force control R2(N=256) - force control R2(N=128) >= 0.03. Headroom-normalised accel_step margin in [0.60, 0.78] in all 3 seeds.
expected_if_false: In >= 2 of 3 seeds, trained force R2 at N=256 is >= 0.04 below the same seed's N=128 value (a real decodability drop), whatever the controls do. If neither branch holds in 2 of 3 seeds, the result is inconclusive.
